title: Coherent objects, topoi and geometric morphisms
statement: Let $\mathcal E$ be a Grothendieck topos [def-weil-pbc-topos], namely a category of sheaves of sets on a small site [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology], in a containing universe [def-weil-size-convention]. An object $A$ is quasi-compact if every family $(A_i\to A)_{i\in I}$ whose coproduct map is an epimorphism has a finite subfamily with epimorphic coproduct map. It is quasi-separated if $B\times_A C$ is quasi-compact whenever $B,C$ are quasi-compact objects with maps to $A$. An object is coherent if it is quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The topos is coherent if it has a small generating full subcategory consisting of coherent objects and closed under finite limits (including the terminal object). Here generating means every object admits an epimorphism from a coproduct of these generators. A geometric morphism $u:\mathcal E'\to\mathcal E$ is an adjunction $u^{-1}\dashv u_*$ with $u^{-1}$ preserving finite limits, as in [def-trf-geometric-morphism]. For coherent topoi $\mathcal E',\mathcal E$, the morphism is coherent if $u^{-1}$ takes coherent objects to coherent objects; it is conservative if $u^{-1}$ reflects isomorphisms.
